courseTitle: Ionic - Build iOS, Android & Web Apps with Ionic & Angular

cues.en: Now of course when there is invalid data entered into our inputs, we might want to do more than just
color the border,
the border at the bottom here red.
Maybe we also want to color the label red and maybe we also want to show a little error message
and that is absolutely possible and something you can do.
For your own error styles for the labels,
just keep in mind that when you do have invalid input here, on the ion-item you get the ion-invalid
and so on classes. So you can use these classes to color the label which is inside of the ion-item appropriately.
So we could set up that styling now in our auth.page.scss file
but maybe we want to have that styling application wide and
therefore I will go to the global.scss file and there, I'll add a new rule that if we have the ion-invalid
class and the ion-touch class, that any ion-label that is nested inside of a component that has
these two classes on it will receive a color, a text color therefore, which is using our ion-color-danger
color,
so this variable here.
If we have a look at the variables real quick, there we'll see that we have our ion-color-danger variable
here which should be red.
So now we assign that variables color to the text color of ion-label inside of a component that has
ion-invalid and ion-touched on it.
So therefore now if I click in there, this label also becomes red
as soon as I'm done touching or working with this input.
So this looks now good,
now also we can show an error message and for this, you simply go into your auth page again
and all we now need is we need to find out whether a given input is invalid or not
and the easiest way of doing that is to assign a local reference to it, here for example e-mail control,
whatever you want to use and that should also be holding a value here and that value should be ngModel
So up here we had ngForm to get access to the form Angular created for us, with ngModel assigned
here,
we get access to the form control Angular created for us
and this has certain fields like the current value but also the current validity
and for that here, we could add a paragraph where we say should be a valid e-mail address and that should
only show up if the e-mail address is invalid.
So I'll add ngIf and check if not e-mail control, using that local reference here, e-mail control is valid
and e-mail control touched, so it should have been touched, the user should have had a chance of
entering something there.
Now when we save that and our application reloads, we see nothing here but if I click in there and out
of there,
now we get that should be a valid e-mail address but of course the positioning is not really that great,
right, it's inside of the input now and that is simply related to the fact how ion-item and ion-label
and ion-input work together.
It works better if we simply put that into its own ion-item here and at the ngIf directive on
the ion-item therefore, like this.
Now if you click in there and out of there, we got this little output here.
Now I'm not a fan of getting that line below that though,
so therefore I'll take advantage of a little attribute I can set on ion-item, I can set lines here to
none so that
this ion-item will not render any visual line and therefore it will just output that text without any lines
and this is now a way better style. Obviously we can now also replace the paragraph here with ion-label,
that is not a must,
you could have kept the paragraph but I actually don't need the extra margins added by the paragraph,
I think it looks a bit nicer if it's just ion-label and we take up less space.
Now let's do the same for the password and of course feel free to do that on your own. I will simply
grab my ion-item here,
copy that
and add it below that ion-item for the password and then on the password,
assign a password control local reference which points at ngModel to get access to the created
form control and
then here, we can replace e-mail control with password control, like that and there, I want to output should at
least be six characters long
or whichever message you want to show,
so now we have our validation in place here.
Last but not least, let's disable the login button if we are in an invalid state and therefore on this
button, on the login button, we can bind the disabled attribute and we want to disable this when the form
is invalid. So we can use our f local reference which remember refers to the overall form and we use
that local reference to check whether this is valid and if it's not valid, then I want to disable the button.
So this is my condition here and I will not watch for the user attaching anything, I will just make
sure if it's not valid, this button is disabled, done and therefore now we start with a disabled button
which has this nice disabled look and can't be clicked.
Awesome.
So with that, we're almost done,
let's now make sure we correctly extract the data when the form is submitted
and of course, make sure that we actually can toggle between login and sign up.
